title: Five Triggers That Could Move Indian Markets This Week: Fed Decision, Q1 Earnings and Oil Prices
excerpt: From the US Federal Reserve's rate decision to the ongoing West Asia conflict, here are the key forces Dalal Street is watching in the last week of July.
body:
• The US Federal Reserve's rate decision on Wednesday is the week's biggest event, with markets pricing in a hold but listening closely for signals on the September meeting.
  • India's Q1 FY27 earnings season continues, with results from major banks, FMCG firms and IT companies expected to shape sector sentiment.
  • Brent crude remains above $100 a barrel amid the US-Iran conflict, putting pressure on India's import bill and current account deficit.
  • Indian markets logged their worst week in four months last week, with the Nifty and Sensex both falling as oil prices and mixed earnings weighed on sentiment.

The Fed Takes Centre Stage

All eyes turn to the US Federal Reserve on Wednesday, when the Federal Open Market Committee concludes its two-day meeting. Markets widely expect the Fed to hold rates steady, but the real action will be in the statement and Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference — where traders will parse every word for hints about whether a September rate cut is on the table.

For Indian markets, the Fed's trajectory matters directly. A dovish signal could drive foreign institutional investor (FII) flows back toward emerging markets, while a hawkish surprise would likely strengthen the dollar and push the rupee lower. The RBI governor's recent assertion that the rupee is undervalued adds a layer of policy tension: if the Fed holds longer, the RBI faces a harder balancing act between growth support and currency stability.

Q1 Earnings: The Report Card Continues

India's April-June quarter earnings season is in full swing, and the results so far have been mixed. Infosys's revenue miss and guidance cut triggered a 5% stock decline, while IDFC First Bank's 132% profit surge showed that pockets of strength remain.

This week brings results from several heavyweight names across banking, FMCG and industrials. Markets will be watching for margin commentary — particularly from companies exposed to higher input costs from elevated crude oil prices — and for management guidance on the second half of the fiscal year.

Oil Prices and the West Asia Wildcard

Brent crude's return above $100 per barrel is perhaps the single biggest headwind for Indian equities this week. The US-Iran conflict continues to disrupt shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea, and Houthi threats have opened a second front in the energy crisis.

India imports roughly 85% of its crude oil, making it acutely sensitive to price spikes. Every $10 increase in crude prices adds an estimated 40-50 basis points to the current account deficit and feeds into inflation, which constrains the RBI's ability to cut rates even as growth concerns mount.

FII Flows and the Rupee

Foreign institutional investors have been net sellers of Indian equities for five consecutive sessions, contributing to the market's losing streak. The combination of elevated oil prices, a strong dollar and geopolitical uncertainty has made emerging market allocators cautious.

The rupee's performance this week will be closely tied to the Fed decision and oil price movements. The RBI has been active in the foreign exchange market, and the recent surge in FCNR(B) deposits — crossing $32 billion — gives it additional ammunition to defend the currency if needed.

What NRI Investors Should Watch

For NRI investors with Indian market exposure, the week presents a concentration of risks and catalysts. The Fed decision's impact on dollar-rupee will directly affect the value of Indian holdings when converted back. Earnings results will set the tone for sectoral bets through the rest of the fiscal year.

The broader question — whether India's premium valuation is justified in a world of $100 oil and uncertain global monetary policy — is the one that will play out over the coming months. This week's data points will be the next set of evidence.
